contests.title: Easton Valley Community School District — Measure LJ: School improvement bonds

provenance.quote:
Shall the Board of Directors of the
Easton Valley Community School
District, in the Counties of Clinton and
Jackson, State of Iowa, be authorized to
contract indebtedness and issue
general obligation bonds in an amount
not exceeding $7,500,000 for the
purposes of acquiring, furnishing,
equipping, constructing, and improving
the School District's school buildings to
include a new gymnasium and new
locker room facilities that include a
FEMA-rated storm shelter, performing
arts upgrades to the existing gym, ADA
updates, and other related building, site
and land improvements?

contests.title: Bellevue — Measure LI: Swimming pool bonds

provenance.quote:
Shall the City of Bellevue, in Jackson
County, State of Iowa, enter into a loan
agreement and issue general obligation
bonds in an amount not exceeding
$3,000,000 for the purpose of paying
the cost, to that extent, of undertaking
the construction, furnishing & equipping
a new municipal swimming pool,
including a splash pad?

contests.title: Decorah — Measure WD: Fire station and city hall financing

provenance.quote:
Shall the City of Decorah, State of
Iowa, issue its General Obligation
Bonds or Capital Loan Notes in an
amount not exceeding the amount of
$20,900,000, in one or more series, for
the purpose of paying costs of
designing, constructing, reconstructing,
enlarging, improving, equipping and
furnishing municipal facilities including a
new fire station and renovation of city
hall, with related site improvements?

contests.title: Spillville — Measure WE: Change uses of local sales tax

provenance.quote:
SHALL THE FOLLOWING PUBLIC
MEASURE BE ADOPTED?
Summary: To authorize a change in the
use of the one percent (1%) local sales
and services tax in the City of Spillville
effective July 1, 2027.
The use of the one percent (1%) local
option sales and services tax shall be
changed in the City of Spillville, effective
July 1, 2027.
PROPOSED USES OF THE TAX:
Revenues from the local option sales
and services tax (LOSST) shall be
allocated as follows:
Zero percent (0%) for property tax relief,
One Hundred percent (100%) will be
allocated annually by the City Council,
for any lawful purpose, including but not
limited to the following purposes:
Capital equipment purchases and
repairs, street, water, sewer and other
capital improvement and maintenance
projects, and/or for assistance to the
Bily Clocks Museum and Antonin
Dvorak Exhibit.
The City of Spillville LOSST fund was
previously established in 1991.  At that
time, its use was limited to street
improvements. This amendment will
broaden the permissible uses of the
LOSST funds, allowing for flexible
planning for the use of LOSST funds,
with the annual LOSST funds to be as
allocated by the City Council, based on
its determination of the City’s changing
annual needs.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes up to $7.5 million in general-obligation bonds for a new gymnasium and locker rooms with a FEMA-rated storm shelter, performing arts upgrades to the existing gym, accessibility updates, and related building, site and land improvements.
Authorizes a loan agreement and up to $3 million in general-obligation bonds to construct, furnish and equip a new municipal swimming pool, including a splash pad.

Authorizes up to $20.9 million in general-obligation bonds or capital loan notes, in one or more series, for municipal facilities including a new fire station, city hall renovations and related site improvements.

Broadens uses of the existing 1% local sales and services tax from street improvements to any lawful city purpose, starting July 1, 2027. The city council would allocate 100% of the annual revenue; 0% is designated for property tax relief. Listed uses include equipment, streets, water, sewer and other improvements, plus assistance for the Bily Clocks Museum and Antonin Dvorak Exhibit.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve broader uses and annual city council allocations.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this change in how the tax can be used.
